# MeshWeave

> Website audit for AI agents: find what prevents AI agents from reading your website correctly. MeshWeave finds the pages, text, and next steps AI agents miss — then tells you what to fix, so agents can understand your site.

MeshWeave answers three questions, in the order an agent meets them: can AI agents reach your site (Reachable), answer from it (Answerable), and act on it (Actionable). Each check scores 0-100 and comes with a fix list ranked by expected score impact.

Why it matters: 94% of B2B buyers used generative AI during their purchase process (6sense, 2025). Agents answer from what they can read on a website, so missing or unclear facts leave gaps in their answers.

Some call this GEO or AEO. MeshWeave covers the site-side part, not AI visibility tracking.

Who it is for: agencies and consultants who audit client websites, and in-house web, SEO, and content teams.

Pricing: an audit is free and needs no sign-in. A free Google sign-in adds private reports, before/after comparison of runs, a downloadable report, and a free API key (up to 25 sites per call) whose report export is unbranded. Expert-guided audits and remediation roadmaps are priced per engagement; ask by email via [Contact](/contact).

[API Reference](/profile#api-access): create a Bearer key in your account profile; endpoint reference lives in [llms-full.txt](/.well-known/llms-full.txt).

[Methodology](/methodology): scoring model, factor weights, and rating bands.

## Checks

Every report scores three checks, each 0-100:

- Reachable — machine context: whether AI crawlers can reach the pages and whether the company is described consistently across them (API fields `geo_score`, `geo_rating`; scale 0-100: Unreachable -> Fully connected).
- Answerable — answer extractability: whether the content states the facts buyers ask about clearly enough for an agent to quote (API fields `aeo_score`, `aeo_rating`; scale 0-100: Not extractable -> Fully extractable).
- Actionable — agent actionability: whether agents can tell what is sold and find how to buy, sign up, or contact the business (API fields `aax_score`, `aax_rating`; scale 0-100: Opaque, meaning an agent cannot tell what to do -> Fluent, meaning the offer and next step are clear).

## API

Two API surfaces. The browser UI uses `/api` endpoints with session auth; the v1 JSON API is Bearer-key authenticated (create a key at `/profile#api-access`).

- `POST /api/v1/analyses` — bulk submit up to 25 pages or sites (Bearer key, durable queue)
- `GET /api/v1/analyses` — list your analyses, cursor-paginated (per-check scores and ratings)
- `GET /api/v1/analyses/{crawl_id}` — site-side contract (factors, weights, ratings, interpretation)
- `GET /api/v1/analyses/{crawl_id}/report.md` — unbranded client-ready report
- `GET /api/v1/analyses/{crawl_id}/diff[.md]` — proof-of-work diff vs the previous revision

Public summary without authentication (same response for owner and anonymous):

- `GET /api/analysis/public/{key}` — JSON summary with scores and ratings (key-scoped, unguessable key)

Account and status pages:
- `/profile#api-access` — API keys (sign in to create a Bearer key)
- `/api/status/{id}` — job status (works without sign-in for public analyses)

Optional pages:
- `/analysis/{key}` — shareable report
- `/analysis/{id}` — private signed-in report
- `/analysis/{id}/diff` — comparison with the previous run
- `/browse` — community analyses

Optional files (agent-discoverable):
- `/robots.txt`, `/sitemap.xml`, `/.well-known/llms.txt` (this file), `/.well-known/llms-full.txt` (full methodology)
